_about: Vesper's clips as keys on her rig (pipeline/sprites/rig.py). A key sets where the body moves (body), how it leans and how the head tilts (degrees), where each wrist goes (near, far) and each hand's shape (nearHand, farHand; farBend turns the fingers up). Motion prompts describe only the body, never the magic: the spell is the stage's effect, drawn over her.

idle-breathe._keys: A breath with a little bob: the body rises more than a real breath would, because the 1.3B model under-follows very small motions (measured in the old game), and the head tips with it.
idle-breathe.motion: standing in place, breathing slowly with a gentle bob, hair and the little cape swaying softly, hands empty and relaxed

cast-light._keys: Chambered at the shoulder, then thrust out at shoulder height, pointing at the foe, held a beat, and recovered inward and down at the side (never a low swing across the front, which reads as an underhand toss: the old game's ADR-0030).
cast-light.motion: she pulls her free hand back to the shoulder, then thrusts her arm straight out toward the right and points, holds it, then lowers it back to her side
cast-light.key_prompt: one arm stretched straight out toward the right at shoulder height, pointing with the index finger, the other hand at her side
cast-light._drawn: The hold is pinned to a drawing of her in it (`keypose`), the way an animator draws the key and leaves the in-betweens. Without one, the first Vesper lost her capelet mid-strike: the video model keeps the costume where a picture pins it.
